requirements.statement: The sign-in page offers a “Forgot password?” link that starts a password reset request.
acceptance_criteria: Given the sign-in page, when a customer selects “Forgot password?”, then a password reset request starts.

requirements.statement: A password reset request returns an identical response whether the account exists or not.
acceptance_criteria: Given otherwise equivalent reset requests for an existing and a nonexistent account, when each request is submitted, then their responses are identical.

requirements.statement: Reset requests are limited to five per account per hour.
acceptance_criteria: Given five reset requests for one account within an hour, when a sixth is made in that hour, then it is not accepted as another reset request for that account.

requirements.statement: A reset link can be used only once.
acceptance_criteria: Given a valid reset link used to complete a reset, when the same link is used again, then another reset cannot be completed with it.

requirements.statement: A reset link expires 30 minutes after issuance.
acceptance_criteria: Given an issued reset link, when it is used at or after 30 minutes from issuance, then it cannot complete a reset.

requirements.statement: A customer can reset the account password with a valid reset link.
acceptance_criteria: Given a valid, unused, unexpired reset link, when the customer completes the reset, then the account password is reset.

requirements.statement: Completing a password reset signs the account out of every active session.
acceptance_criteria: Given an account with multiple active sessions, when its password reset completes, then none of those sessions remains signed in.

requirements.statement: The account owner is notified after every successful password reset.
acceptance_criteria: Given a completed password reset, when it succeeds, then the account owner receives a notification for that reset.
